newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Japan mission in Hong Kong seeks police protection.
newsitem.headline: Japan mission in Hong Kong seeks police protection.

text.p: Japan's diplomatic mission in Hong Kong said on Thursday it had asked for police protection, fearing a backlash after a Hong Kong activist drowned during a protest against Japan's claim to a disputed chain of islands.
"Yes, today we asked for protection, not only for our office but all Japanese organisations," an official at the Japanese Consulate in Hong Kong said.
The official said the request covered all Japanese organisations in the territory, including private companies.

Hong Kong activist David Chan, leader of 18 protesters aboard the Kien Hwa 2, died on Thursday after leaping into the East China Sea along with four others to defy a blockade of the Diaoyu islands by Japanese coast guard vessels.
The Japanese official also said the consulate had received numerous calls in recent weeks from Japanese living in the territory expressing concern for their own safety.
Hong Kong has been swept by Chinese nationalistic fervour for weeks since Japanese activists planted symbols of sovereignty on the islands, known in Japan as the Senkakus.
China, Taiwan and Japan all claim sovereignty of the islands.

There have been no known attacks or threats on Japanese or Japan's diplomatic mission in Hong Kong, apart from the public protests against Japan's claims to the islands in recent weeks and calls by protestors to boycott Japanese products.
Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.
Tokyo's claim to islands dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
